active case finding and prompt treatment can be used to reduce TB transmission.
active case-finding of tuberculosis (TB) patients and prompt treatment of those found to have active TB disease are effective strategies to prevent TB transmission.

the evidence from these studies is sufficient to support the conclusion that active case-finding is effective for reducing TB transmission.

the use of a combination of active case-finding, treatment and prevention strategies, including a high-quality, well-functioning health system, is the best way to reduce the incidence and prevalence of TB and to reduce the burden on the healthcare system.

the evidence from the studies included in the review supports the use of the following interventions to prevent transmission of TB in the community: active case finding and treatment of smear positive cases, active case finding and contact tracing and treatment of smear negative cases and treatment of smear-positive cases with the short course chemotherapy regimen.

the TB epidemic can be turned around.

we can prevent the spread of tuberculosis by identifying and treating people with TB early, before they have a chance to infect others.
